---
title: Add the chat
description: Put an assistant on the page that does things, not just answers. The model runs on your server with the key; every tool call runs in the browser, under the agent cursor.
sidebar:
  label: 8. Add the chat
---

`<AgentChat>` is a chat widget whose agent works the **live page** through its tools. The model runs on your server,
behind a route at `/api/chat`, with the API key there: Claude by default, or any model the Vercel AI SDK reaches. Every
tool call runs **in the browser**, so the cursor plays exactly as it does for any agent, and anything gated on a click
waits for the person.

## A complete example

Install the chat, and the AI SDK package of your model's provider (server side only):

```package-install
npm install @webmcp-agents/chat
```

```package-install
npm install @ai-sdk/anthropic
```

Then two pieces: the widget inside your provider, and the `/api/chat` route. The highlighted lines are the ones you
add.

<View title="Vite">

<include meta='title="src/main.tsx" {1,8-9,17-22}'>/_examples/vite/src/main.chat.tsx</include>

In development, the Vite plugin serves `/api/chat` from the dev server. Add it to the config you have:

```ts vite.config.ts
import { webAgentsChatDev } from "@webmcp-agents/chat/vite"; // [!code highlight]
import { agents } from "./src/agents"; // [!code highlight]

// In defineConfig({ … }):
plugins: [react(), tailwindcss(), webAgentsChatDev({ agents })], // [!code highlight]
```

It reads the key from `.env.local` on the server side, and refuses to start when a `VITE_` variable is named like a
secret. In production, `/api/chat` is a function of your host's. On Vercel, a file in `api/` is one:

<include meta='title="api/chat.ts"'>/_examples/vite/api/chat.ts</include>

</View>

<View title="Next.js">

<include meta='title="app/providers.tsx" {3,7-8,11,17-22}'>/_examples/nextjs/app/providers.chat.tsx</include>

`/api/chat` is a route handler, in development and in production:

<include meta='title="app/api/chat/route.ts"'>/_examples/nextjs/app/api/chat/route.ts</include>

To make sure the key can never reach a client component, read it in a module that starts with
`import "server-only"` and taint it with React's `experimental_taintUniqueValue`, as `apps/nextjs/lib/env.server.ts`
does ([Field Store on Next.js](/examples/nextjs)). The taint APIs are behind a flag: set `experimental: { taint: true }` in
`next.config.ts`.

</View>

<View title="TanStack Start">

<include meta='title="src/components/providers.tsx" {1,5-6,9,15-20}'>/_examples/tanstack-start/src/components/providers.chat.tsx</include>

`/api/chat` is a server route, in development and in production:

<include meta='title="src/routes/api/chat.ts"'>/_examples/tanstack-start/src/routes/api/chat.ts</include>

No example app runs TanStack Start: this route is type-checked against `@tanstack/react-start` 1.169, not run. The
server-route API has moved between Start releases, so check it against the version you install.

Start's dev server serves the route, so no Vite plugin is needed for it. You can still add `webAgentsChatDev()` for its
secret guard (it refuses to start when a `VITE_` variable is named like a secret); give its `path` option something
unused, so it never shadows the real route.

</View>

<View title="Astro">

<include meta='title="src/components/providers.tsx" {1,5-6,9,15-20}'>/_examples/astro/src/components/providers.chat.tsx</include>

`/api/chat` is an endpoint rendered on demand, so the site needs a server adapter (Node, Vercel, Netlify…):

<include meta='title="src/pages/api/chat.ts"'>/_examples/astro/src/pages/api/chat.ts</include>

This site is built with Astro but has no chat, so this endpoint is type-checked, not run in a real app.

</View>

`<AgentChat agent={shopper}>` needs no adapter: it talks to `/api/chat`. The route serves the same `agents` the page
uses, because the browser sends only the agent's id and the server reads the instructions from its own copy.

## The key

Put the key in `.env.local`, at the root of the project:

```bash .env.local
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-…
```

It is read on the server only. **Never give it a public prefix**: `VITE_` (Vite, TanStack Start), `NEXT_PUBLIC_`
(Next.js) or `PUBLIC_` (Astro). Those variables are copied into the JavaScript the browser downloads.

Without a key the widget says "Chat isn't configured on this site", and the rest of the page works as before.

## Pick a model

One variable on the server picks the model, as `"<provider>/<model>"`, and the provider's own SDK is used when its
key is set (install it beside `@webmcp-agents/chat`). Without the SDK, the AI Gateway built into the AI SDK serves any
id with one key.

```bash .env.local
WEB_AGENTS_MODEL=openai/gpt-5.5
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-…
```

| Prefix | Package | Key |
|---|---|---|
| `anthropic/` (the default: `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`) | `@ai-sdk/anthropic` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
| `openai/` | `@ai-sdk/openai` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| `google/` | `@ai-sdk/google` | `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY` |
| `deepseek/` | `@ai-sdk/deepseek` | `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` |
| `xai/` | `@ai-sdk/xai` | `XAI_API_KEY` |
| `mistral/` | `@ai-sdk/mistral` | `MISTRAL_API_KEY` |
| `openrouter/<vendor>/<model>` | `@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider` | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` |
| any other `a/b` id | none (the AI Gateway) | `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` |

An agent's own `model` ([Define an agent](/build/define-an-agent#a-model-per-agent)) beats this default.

## How a turn runs

The server runs **one model step per request**; tools run in the browser between steps.

1. The widget sends the conversation and the page's current tools (names, descriptions, schemas) to `/api/chat`.
2. The model answers with text or with tool calls.
3. The widget runs each tool call on the page, under the cursor, and shows it in the conversation.
4. It waits for the page's tools to settle (a navigation brings new ones), then sends the results back for the next
   step.

A failed tool never ends the run: the result goes back to the model with its [error code](/concepts/errors). The
person's **Stop** cancels the call in progress. If the run itself fails (the model, the network), **Try again** resumes
from the last tool call that finished, so nothing is done twice.

The route refuses browser requests from other sites, but anyone can still call it directly. A public deployment needs
a `guard` with rate limits and a daily budget: [Deploy](/more/deploy) has one.

## Try it

Start the app with the key in `.env.local`, open the chat (bottom left in development) and ask:

> What's in my cart?

The model calls `get_cart`, the call shows in the conversation, and the answer names the Ocean Tee. On the page with
your `<AddToCart />` form, ask "Add two more in size L": the cursor types into the form, and the chat shows the call.

## Options you'll use most

| `<AgentChat>` prop | What it is for |
|---|---|
| `agent` | The [agent](/build/define-an-agent): its instructions, its tools and its helpers. Default: every tool on the page. |
| `layout` | `"docked"` (default), a full-height panel the page makes room for, or `"floating"`. A bottom sheet on phones. |
| `position` | `"bottom-right"` (default) or `"bottom-left"`. |
| `suggestions` | Starter prompts. Default: made from the page's tools. |
| `adapters` | Several models with a switcher, such as Claude and an [on-device model](/more/on-device-agent). |

| `createChatHandler` option | What it is for |
|---|---|
| `agents` | The top-level agents it serves. |
| `model` | The default model. Default: `WEB_AGENTS_MODEL`, else `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`. |
| `maxSteps` | Tool steps per message. Default 8. |
| `guard`, `beforeModel` | Rate limits, origin checks, budgets. |

Every option: [`<AgentChat>`](/reference/chat/agent-chat), [`createChatHandler`](/reference/chat/create-chat-handler)
and [`webAgentsChatDev`](/reference/chat/web-agents-chat-dev). To render the chat with your own shadcn/ui components
instead of the built-in widget, see [shadcn chat blocks](/more/shadcn-chat-blocks).
